challenges.name: cpu-bound-strategy-quiz
challenges.title: Chunking, worker threads or cluster?
challenges.description: Three tools, three different problems. Pick the one that actually removes the blocking - and spot the claims that sound right but are not.

questions.question: POST /fraud/score-batch spends about 400 ms of pure JavaScript CPU per call (an in-memory scoring model). While it runs, the p99 of POST /payments on the same instance jumps from 40 ms to 450 ms. The service is a single Node.js process on a 4 vCPU VM. Which change best fixes /payments latency while keeping scoring throughput?
questions.explanation: The scoring is CPU work on the main thread, so every other request waits until it finishes. A worker_threads pool moves it off the event loop and uses the idle cores, and a bounded queue stops a burst of batches from piling up unbounded. Marking the function async changes nothing - the CPU work still runs synchronously on the same thread. process.nextTick callbacks run before the event loop gets back to I/O, so they do not let /payments in. Cluster spreads requests across processes, but any /payments request that lands on the process currently scoring still waits the full 400 ms.

options.text: Declare the scoring function async and await it in the handler, so it no longer blocks.
Run the scoring in a worker_threads pool (for example piscina) sized to the spare cores, with a bounded queue.
Start 4 processes with cluster: the load is spread, so scoring can no longer delay a payment.
Call process.nextTick() every 100 transactions inside the scoring loop to let other requests run.

questions.question: Which statements are true? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: cluster forks full processes: each has its own heap and event loop and the primary hands out connections on the shared port. Worker threads are separate V8 isolates - they do not see each other's variables and communicate through postMessage (structured clone), transferred ArrayBuffers or a SharedArrayBuffer. Chunking does not reduce the total CPU time - it only interleaves other callbacks between chunks, which is enough when the work is moderate. Creating a Worker costs milliseconds and several MB of memory, so a reusable pool beats one Worker per request.

options.text: cluster forks separate processes that share the listening port; each has its own memory and its own event loop.
Worker threads share one JavaScript heap, so a worker can read the main thread's variables directly.
Chunking with setImmediate keeps all work on the main thread: total CPU time stays the same, but other requests are served between chunks.
Spawning a new Worker for every request is cheaper than keeping a pool, because threads are lightweight.

challenges.name: process-in-chunks
challenges.title: Score a batch in chunks without freezing the API
challenges.description: Write processInChunks(items, chunkSize, fn, yieldToLoop): run the synchronous scoring fn over every item in order, at most chunkSize items at a time, and await yieldToLoop() between chunks so waiting HTTP requests get served. The harness simulates requests arriving mid-batch and measures how long they wait.

tests.name: 10 transactions in chunks of 3: requests wait at most one chunk
A request waiting before the batch starts is served after the first chunk
A batch smaller than one chunk runs in a single go
An empty batch resolves with an empty array
12 transactions in chunks of 4: exact chunk boundaries
